question.problem: Given that the continuous random variable $V$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-2,0],$ compute $P(V\le -\frac{1}{2}).$
question.worked_solution:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $V$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

$$
f(v)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{b-a},\, & a\le v\le b, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Our random variable $V$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-2,0],$ so it has the following probability density function:

$$
f(v)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2},\, & -2\le v\le 0, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(V\le -\frac{1}{2}) & =P(-2\le V\le -\frac{1}{2}) \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1/2}f(v)\,\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1/2}\frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}v \\  & =\frac{-\frac{1}{2}-(-2)}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
